cover: The cover of Democratizing Linux: A Pipe Dream. A penguin in a nightcap sleeps on an ice floe and dreams of a desktop computer with a penguin on its screen, under the words the year of the Linux desktop. Beside it a dumpster is on fire, with a broken four-pane window sticking out of it. The dumpster is labelled teraSlop, and a sign reads: the evolution of spyware, vapourware and bloatware.
ch01: Flange, a penguin in a hard hat, feeds the bytes of the word hello into a pipe. They come out of the other end in the same order, where a gopher is waiting to catch them.
ch02: Docket, a gopher, stands at a wall of pigeonholes numbered 0 to 5. Holes 0, 1 and 2 hold tickets for the terminal, and a string runs from the ticket in hole 3 to a filing cabinet.
ch03: Fork, a small red daemon, holds a fork. Beside it stands a smaller copy of itself, just created. Tags give their numbers: 500 for the parent and 501 for the child.
ch04: Conch, a hermit crab, lives in a shell and types at a terminal. The screen shows a pipeline, and behind the terminal 3 small penguins stand in a row, each passing a fish to the next.
ch05: Klaxon, an owl, is the night watch. Signal flags numbered 2, 9 and 15 fly from a mast, a bell rings, and a hare that was asleep jumps awake.
ch06: Tick, a gnu in a referee's shirt, holds a stopwatch over a single running lane. A hare and a tortoise wait their turn, and the bib with the smallest number runs next.
ch07: Atlas, an elephant, draws a map divided into numbered pages with a pencil held in its trunk. Most squares are blank, a few are filled in, and one is being drawn now that it is needed.
ch08: Stash, a squirrel, keeps the pages it read most recently on a shelf within reach and holds an acorn. The full store is a hollow in a distant tree, a longer trip that the shelf saves.
ch09: Relay, an octopus wearing a headset, works a switchboard. 2 lamps on the board are lit, and an arm reaches to each of them. The other lines are left alone.
ch10: Halyard and Cleat, 2 carrier pigeons on separate posts, face each other. Notes numbered 1, 2 and 3 travel along a line between them, in order.
ch11: 3 cats sit in 3 cardboard boxes. Every box is marked number 1, and each cat is sure it is the first. An owl on a branch above can see all 3.
ch12: Weir, a beaver in a hard hat, has built a dam. A mark on the dam shows the limit, the water stands exactly at the mark, and no more is let through.
ch13: A whale carries shipping containers on its back across the sea. A penguin, a gopher and a crab ride on top, and the middle container has a window through which a small igloo can be seen.
crab-moods: 4 crabs show what a write to a pipe can meet. A happy crab: the ring has room, and the bytes go in. A sleeping crab: the ring is full, and the writer sleeps. An angry crab: no reader is left, and the write fails with EPIPE. A cute crab: the writer closes its end, and the reader sees the end of the stream.
